label: late original-phase token from {j,f,z,v,1,t,p} after a prefix rich in {h,2,g,y,l,b,0}
explanation: Almost entirely an original-phase unit (98.8% of mass). It never fires at t=0-2, and its rate climbs from orig_idx 3 to a peak around orig_idx 5-7. It looks like a soft conjunction of two token groups: (a) the earlier prefix contains several of h,2,g,y,l,b,0, and the effect is strongest when the first token is one of these (first_tok h or 2 gives about 4.5x lift); (b) the current input is one of j,f,z,v (about 4.5x), or more weakly 1,t,p. The current input is usually the first occurrence of that token. The largest activations (top quartile) are sequences that open with two or more group-(a) tokens followed by j/f/z. It is weak and rare at the <DEL> step and essentially silent in the copy phase. The firing rate is never higher than about 6% in any single bin, so the boundary looks graded rather than crisp. The predicate gets about 0.32 precision and 0.71 mass recall on dev. Requiring first_tok in group (a) raises F1 to 0.47 but lowers mass recall to 0.55.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=h (+3.41), orig0=2 (+3.28), in_tok=f (+3.22), in_tok=z (+3.18), orig1=h (+2.97), orig1=2 (+2.96). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-7.78), phase=2 (-5.78), in_tok=b (-4.41), in_tok=h (-4.03).
